ast.description: Client and server configuration files (.cfg, .rc) parsed by exec at startup or runtime.
Bitmap or texture font used to render console and HUD text. Loaded via gl_font / R_RegisterPic on the charset path.
User-selectable crosshair overlay image.
World, model, HUD, or shader textures. Includes 32-bit replacements (.tga/.png/.jpg) and original .pcx data.
Q3-style shader script (.shader) or runtime-registered shader via R_RegisterShader / R_LoadShader. FTE-specific surface; no ezQuake counterpart.
Player model skin, loaded per-connect from userinfo. Includes .pcx and .skin (Q3-style alias) variants.
Audio samples consumed by the sound engine (.wav, .ogg, .mp3).
3D model (.mdl, .md3, .md2, .iqm). Brush models are categorized as 'map' instead.
Level geometry (.bsp). Downloaded per-connect when absent.

Per-map auxiliary files loaded alongside a .bsp: potentially-hearable sets (.phs), leaf-visibility extensions (.lvx), and similar BSP companions. Distinct from map_lighting (.lit) which is the colored-lighting companion.
Per-map colored-lighting companion (.lit) loaded alongside a .bsp.
Heightmap data (.hms, .hmp) consumed by FTE's terrain renderer.
Legacy Quake asset archive (.wad) containing textures or HUD graphics.
Original Quake pack archive (.pak). Mounted into search path at init.
ZIP-based pack archive (.pk3, .pk4, .zip). Mounted into search path at init.
Recorded game replay (.qwd, .mvd, .dem, .qtv).
Compressed demo archive (.dz). Decoded via DZip before playback.
Captured screen image (.tga, .png, .jpg) emitted by SCR_ScreenShot and friends.
User-configurable HUD graphic referenced by a hud_* cvar or registered via R_RegisterPic. Includes .lmp legacy overlays.
Six-image cubemap for the world sky, selected by r_skyname.
Console and match logs (.log).
Team-reporting location file (.loc) keyed to a map name; used by %l macros and TP_LoadLocFile.
Compiled QuakeC bytecode (qwprogs.dat, spprogs.dat, csqc progs, mod progs). Includes Q3-style .qvm bytecode loaded by FTE's QuakeVM.
Sprite model (.spr). Distinct from .mdl via the precache path.
Gettext-style translation files (.po) consumed by FTE's localization layer.
Single-player save data (.sav).
Native plugin DLL/SO (FTE's fteplug_*.dll family). Loaded via the plug command.
Files the taxonomy doesn't otherwise cover. Includes generic data lists (.txt, .lst), pak listings, and miscellaneous engine-internal files.

asset_extensions.notes: Q3-style alias-skin reference file; lives under models/<model>/<name>.skin.
Q3-style QuakeC virtual-machine bytecode; FTE QuakeVM consumes this alongside .dat progs.
Generic text data; too varied to categorize meaningfully.
List files including pak.lst and similar engine-internal listings.

asset_path_rules.description: For the QuakeWorld game (manifest selector "-quake"/"q1"), FTE's gamemode_info[] entry defines the base game directory set as id1/, qw/, and *fte/ (the asterisk marks a private gamedir). When the manifest selector resolves, FS_Manifest_SetDefaultSettings copies the gamepath array into the manifest. FS_ChangeGame later iterates gamepath[] calling FS_AddGameDirectory for each base dir; each call pushes the dir to the head of com_searchpaths via FS_AddPathHandle. Effective lookup order is *fte > qw > id1 (last added is highest precedence in the LIFO stack).

com_searchpaths is a singly-linked list traversed head-first. FS_FLocateFile walks `for (search = com_searchpaths ; search ; search = search->next)` and returns the first FindFile match. Every FS_AddPathHandle call inserts at the head, so the most recently added directory or archive is checked first.

After mounting all base gamepath entries (id1, qw, *fte for QW), FS_ChangeGame snapshots com_searchpaths into com_base_searchpaths. Subsequent `gamedir` swaps unwind paths above this snapshot but preserve the base stack -- so id1, qw, *fte always remain mounted.

FS_RegisterDefaultFileSystems registers archive backends in this order: dz, pak, pk3, pk4, pkz, pkx, iwd, apk, zip, kpf. Later- registered kinds are scanned later in FS_AddDataFiles, and each scan's matches push onto the LIFO searchpath stack. Net effect for QW: pk4 > pk3 > pak. Quake 1 / QuakeWorld installs rarely use pk4; in practice this collapses to pk3 > pak.

Within a game directory FS_AddDataFiles loads pak0.<ext>, pak1.<ext>, pak2.<ext>, ... in numeric-ascending order until one is missing. Because each is pushed to the head of com_searchpaths on load, higher-numbered paks end up earlier in lookup order. Effect: pak1.pak overrides pak0.pak for same-name entries. Same loop runs per archive kind (pak, pk3, pk4).

If a file named `pak.lst` exists in the game directory, FS_AddDataFiles parses it for an explicit pak-load ordering before the numbered-pak scan. Names listed there are loaded by FS_AddSingleDataFile in file order. Unlike ezQuake's pak.lst (which suppresses the wildcard scan entirely), FTE's pak.lst is additive: numbered + manifest + wildcard scans all still run after the pak.lst entries.

After loading the numbered pakN.<ext> series and any manifest- declared packages, FS_AddDataFiles enumerates `*.<ext>` in the same directory and pushes each match to the head of com_searchpaths. Wildcard-discovered archives sit higher on the stack than numbered paks of the same extension and so take precedence.

FS_AddGameDirectory pushes the directory itself onto com_searchpaths (via FS_AddPathHandle). FS_AddPathHandle then triggers FS_AddDataFiles which pushes archives within that directory on top. Net effect: archives override loose files in the same directory.

`gamedir <mod>` and `-game <mod>` both route through FS_ChangeGame, which loads a fresh manifest (or alters the existing one) and rebuilds the searchpath stack. Old searchpaths above com_base_searchpaths are freed; the base stack survives. The new mod directory is mounted via FS_AddGameDirectory on top of the base.

After mounting a mod dir, lookups for assets missing in the mod fall through to the next searchpath entries -- which are the base stack (qw, id1 for QW). This works automatically because FS_FLocateFile's LIFO walk continues past head when FindFile misses; mod directory was pushed last so it's consulted first, but absent matches fall through to the next entry.
`-basedir <path>` overrides the auto-detected base directory (where id1/, qw/, and *fte/ are searched). Checked during init; when present, base game directories are resolved relative to this value.
`-game <mod>` (or `+gamedir <mod>` at the console) calls FS_ChangeGame to mount the named mod gamedir on top of the base stack. Equivalent to running `gamedir <mod>` immediately after init.

`-quake` selects FTE's QuakeWorld game manifest (id1/qw/*fte gamepath set, QUAKEPROT protocol, q1 mode key). FTE supports multiple game manifests via cmdline selectors (-quake, -quake2, -quake3, -hexen2, etc.); -quake is the QW-relevant one. The manifest's installation string is matched against gamemode_info[i].argname inside FS_Manifest_SetDefaultSettings, which then copies the gamepath set into the manifest.
